headline_marked: [[World's first 3D-printed RC jet takes flight]], aims for Mach 0.8 world record
headline: World's first 3D-printed RC jet takes flight, aims for Mach 0.8 world record
summary: The Kingchaser, made from PETG and PPS-CF, aims to break the 9-year-old Guinness World Record for fastest model aircraft. It's designed to hit 614 mph (988 km/h).
details: The Kingchaser, a 3D-printed jet-powered remote-controlled aircraft, has completed its maiden flight. Constructed from PETG, PPS-CF, carbon-fiber rods, and aluminum, it targets Mach 0.8 (614 mph or 988 km/h) to break the world speed record for model aircraft.

The Mach Initiative, a team of University of Bath graduates, developed the Kingchaser. Their journey began with the smaller Kinglet prototype, which used an Electric Ducted Fan (EDF) and a modular design for rapid iteration.

The next stage was the Kingfisher, a meter-long aircraft powered by a Jetcat P60 miniature jet turbine, capable of 63 N·m of thrust and reaching 205 mph (330 km/h). This model focused on achieving stable jet flight rather than breaking records, necessitating significant design changes from the Kinglet.

The Kingchaser is 20% larger than the Kingfisher and features substantial design modifications. Its external construction is mostly PETG, with the engine housing upgraded to PPS-CF, reinforced with carbon fiber, aluminum, and steel to withstand extreme forces.

To protect against the engine's heat, the Kingchaser incorporates titanium exhaust sheets and aluminum tape. The internal aluminum skeleton was replaced with carbon fiber rods to reduce weight and minimize custom-CNC machined parts.

The aircraft is equipped with a fully instrumented avionics system for comprehensive telemetry collection and an FPV system for enhanced piloting at high speeds. High-torque 70 kg-cm servos control the elevons, providing the necessary force for precise maneuvers.
While no official date has been announced for the record attempt, The Mach Initiative regularly posts entertaining build logs on their YouTube channel, allowing enthusiasts to follow their progress.

topic: watersheep open source ai alternative to jev
headline_marked: [[WaterSheep launches as open-source alternative to TypeSafe's Jev]] with Python SDK compatibility
headline: WaterSheep launches as open-source alternative to TypeSafe's Jev with Python SDK compatibility
summary: WaterSheep is an open-source decision-making model, mirroring Jev's API for seamless integration with TypeSafe's Python SDK. It offers calibrated probabilities for automated decision-making.
details: WaterSheep is an open-source alternative to TypeSafe's Jev, a model designed for decision-making rather than text generation. It processes state and typed questions to return choices, scores, and probabilities.
It mimics Jev's POST /v1/systemone API request and response shape, allowing direct use with TypeSafe's Python SDK (tested with 0.7.2). Any API key works locally for testing.
The model achieves 77.8% accuracy on in-distribution test splits and 61.2% on held-out datasets. Its probabilities are calibrated, enabling thresholds for automated actions or human review.
WaterSheep runs as ONNX and offers a live demo. It is English-only, truncates long inputs, and performs weakest on rating questions. It's not intended for high-stakes decisions alone.
The code, weights, and training pipeline are available under Apache 2.0 license. Users can retrain the model on their own data with a single script.
caption:
WaterSheep, a new open-source decision-making model, directly replaces TypeSafe's Jev. It's compatible with Jev's Python SDK and offers calibrated probabilities for automated actions.

WaterSheep is an open-source alternative to TypeSafe's Jev, a model designed for decision-making rather than text generation. It processes state and typed questions to return choices, scores, and probabilities.

It mimics Jev's POST /v1/systemone API request and response shape, allowing direct use with TypeSafe's Python SDK (tested with 0.7.2). Any API key works locally for testing.

The model achieves 77.8% accuracy on in-distribution test splits and 61.2% on held-out datasets. Its probabilities are calibrated, enabling thresholds for automated actions or human review.

WaterSheep runs as ONNX and offers a live demo. It is English-only, truncates long inputs, and performs weakest on rating questions. It's not intended for high-stakes decisions alone.

The code, weights, and training pipeline are available under Apache 2.0 license. Users can retrain the model on their own data with a single script.
